items.followUp: What are photosynthetic pigments, and what do they absorb?

rubric.why: Identifies that these pigments absorb light energy used in photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the pigments absorb light energy used in photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Shows what the pigments are or gives a relevant example.
rubric.description: Identifies them as light-absorbing substances or gives chlorophyll as an example
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing them as light-absorbing substances or naming chlorophyll.

modelAnswer: Photosynthetic pigments are light-absorbing substances in cells that capture light energy for photosynthesis.
Chlorophyll is the main photosynthetic pigment.

items.followUp: Name the two main types of fermentation and state one product of each.

rubric.why: Names one major type of fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming alcoholic fermentation.

rubric.why: Names the other major type of fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming lactic acid fermentation.

modelAnswer: Two types of fermentation are alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.

items.followUp: What is the optimum temperature of an enzyme?

rubric.why: States that optimum pH corresponds to the greatest enzyme activity.
rubric.description: The enzyme has maximum activity at this pH
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzyme activity is maximum or greatest at this pH.

rubric.why: Identifies the condition being defined as pH.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the pH at which the enzyme works best.

modelAnswer: Optimum pH is the pH at which an enzyme shows its maximum activity.

items.followUp: How are enzymes used in the textile industry?

rubric.why: Identifies the use of enzymes in removing ink during paper recycling.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are used to remove ink or de-ink recycled paper.

rubric.why: Places the use in the paper industry or paper recycling process.
rubric.description: Links the process to paper making or recycling
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying paper making or recycling as the context.

modelAnswer: In the paper industry, enzymes are used to remove ink from recycled paper.
This de-inking helps produce cleaner, brighter paper.

items.followUp: Name two vitamins that act as coenzymes.

rubric.why: Names one B vitamin that can act as a coenzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a coenzyme-forming B vitamin, such as B1 or B2.
Award 1 mark for naming another coenzyme-forming B vitamin.

modelAnswer: Two vitamins that act as coenzymes are vitamin B₁ (thiamine) and vitamin B₂ (riboflavin).

items.followUp: What pH conditions are needed for pepsin to work effectively?

rubric.why: States the acidic conditions produced by hydrochloric acid.
rubric.description: Hydrochloric acid makes the stomach contents acidic
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HCl provides an acidic medium or low pH.

rubric.why: Connects the acidic medium with pepsin activity.
rubric.description: The acidic medium enables pepsin to work effectively
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that pepsin works effectively or digests proteins in this acidic medium.

modelAnswer: Hydrochloric acid makes the stomach contents acidic.
This acidic medium provides the suitable pH for pepsin to digest proteins.

items.followUp: What is angioplasty, and what is its purpose?

rubric.why: Identifies vascular surgery as a surgical procedure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as surgery or a surgical procedure.
Award 1 mark for stating that the procedure involves blood vessels.

modelAnswer: Vascular surgery is surgery performed on blood vessels.
It is used to repair or treat damaged or diseased blood vessels.

items.followUp: Describe how the structure of a villus helps absorption in the small intestine.

rubric.why: Identifies the location and characteristic shape of villi.
rubric.description: Finger-like projections in the small intestine
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing villi as finger-like projections of the small intestine.

rubric.why: States the main function of villi in absorption.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that villi increase the surface area for absorbing digested food.

modelAnswer: Villi are tiny finger-like projections present on the inner lining of the small intestine.
They increase the surface area for absorption of digested food into the blood.
